scheduled.status: The commission's information sheet (revised 08/06/2026) gives the date. The council's July 7, 2026 agenda listed 'Proposed Language for Rule 103, International Building Code (IBC), 2024 Edition' and 'Rule 111, International Plumbing Code (IPC), 2024 Edition' on its consent agenda. The final rule and the Louisiana amendments to the 2024 editions were NOT found or read; a September 2026 emergency rule still amends the 2021 IPC. Everything below describes the 2021 editions in force today.

governing_table.code: Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code: International Plumbing Code with Louisiana amendments (LAC 17:I.111). The building code's Chapter 29 points to it.
governing_table.table: Table 403.1, Minimum Number of Required Plumbing Fixtures
governing_table.quote: Plumbing fixtures shall be provided in the minimum number as shown in Table 403.1, based on the actual use of the building or space. Uses not shown in Table 403.1 shall be considered individually by the code official. The number of occupants shall be determined by the International Building Code.
governing_table.note: Louisiana's IBC amendment (official blue book, LAC 17:I.103): 'Adopt Chapter 29: All plumbing provisions located in this Chapter shall reference 2021 IPC with Louisiana Amendments.' The Louisiana amendments to Table 403.1 change only footnotes e (service sinks) and f (swimming pools); the office, restaurant and school rows are the model code's. Amendments read on the official blue book; the table rows themselves on UpCodes (the ICC's own site returned 403).

cities_may_amend_quote.quote: all municipalities and parishes in this state shall enforce only the Uniform Construction Code provided in this Chapter and as promulgated in the commission's rules and regulations. ... Nothing in this Chapter allows any local government to avoid enforcement, or to otherwise amend any of the mandatory construction code provisions required in this Chapter
cities_may_amend_quote.cite: La. R.S. 37:3737(A)(1), as printed in the commission's blue book of August 1, 2026

office.row_label: Business: Buildings for the transaction of business, professional services, other services involving merchandise, office buildings, banks, ambulatory care, light industrial and similar uses
office.wc_male: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.wc_female: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50
office.quote: 1 per 25 for the first 50 and 1 per 50 for the remainder exceeding 50

restaurant.row_label: Assembly: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts (footnote d)
restaurant.quote: Restaurants, banquet halls and food courts | 1 per 75 | 1 per 75 | 1 per 200 | — | 1 per 500 | 1 service sink. Footnote d: The occupant load for seasonal outdoor seating and entertainment areas shall be included when determining the minimum number of facilities required.

school.quote: Educational facilities | 1 per 50 | 1 per 50 | — | 1 per 100 | 1 service sink

sex_split.text: The occupant load is divided in half, one half for each sex, unless approved statistical data show another split.
sex_split.quote: To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. ... Exceptions: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicate a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

rounding.text: Fractions round up to the next whole number. The table's footnote a also counts any fraction of the stated number of people as needing a fixture.
rounding.quote: Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number.

urinal_substitution.text: Urinals are optional. In each toilet room they may replace up to 67% of the required toilets in assembly and educational buildings and up to 50% in all other buildings. Each urinal needs partitions (screens) at least 60 inches high.
urinal_substitution.quote: 424.2 Substitution for Water Closets. In each bathroom or toilet room, urinals shall not be substituted for more than 67 percent of the required water closets in assembly and educational occupancies. Urinals shall not be substituted for more than 50 percent of the required water closets in all other occupancies. | 405.3.5 Urinal Partitions. Each urinal utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate area with walls or partitions to provide privacy. ... The walls or partitions shall begin at a height not greater than 12 inches (305 mm) from and extend not less than 60 inches (1524 mm) above the finished floor surface.

small_occupancy_exception.text: Separate men's and women's rooms are not required where the total occupant load is 15 or fewer, in shops of 100 or fewer, or in business occupancies of 25 or fewer. Louisiana adds: existing tenant spaces under 1,800 sq ft classed as business or mercantile.
small_occupancy_exception.quote: Separate facilities shall not be required in structures or tenant spaces with a total occupant load, including both employees and customers, of 15 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in mercantile occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 100 or fewer. Separate facilities shall not be required in business occupancies in which the maximum occupant load is 25 or fewer. ... Separate facilities shall not be required for existing tenant spaces under 1800 sq. ft. where the occupancy classification is either B or M.

occupant_load.text: Office (business areas): 150 gross sq ft per person. Restaurant dining room (assembly, tables and chairs): 15 net sq ft per person. Classroom: 20 net sq ft per person.
occupant_load.quote: TABLE 1004.5 MAXIMUM FLOOR AREA ALLOWANCES PER OCCUPANT: Assembly without fixed seats, Unconcentrated (tables and chairs) 15 net | Business areas 150 gross | Educational, Classroom area 20 net

stall_per_toilet.text: Every toilet used by the public or employees needs its own compartment with a door, except in a single-occupant room with a lockable door.
stall_per_toilet.quote: 405.3.4 Water Closet Compartment. Each water closet utilized by the public or employees shall occupy a separate compartment with walls or partitions and a door enclosing the fixtures to ensure privacy. Exceptions: Water closet compartments shall not be required in a single-occupant toilet room with a lockable door.

schools_extra.text: Louisiana amendment: in schools, boys' and girls' toilet rooms must be within 200 feet of any classroom door (children through age 12) or 400 feet (secondary), and on each floor of a multi-story building.
schools_extra.quote: For primary schools ... for children through 12 years of age, separate boys' and girls' toilet room doors shall not be further than 200 feet from any classroom doors. For secondary schools ... shall not be further than 400 feet from any classroom door. In multi- storied buildings, there shall be boys' and girls' toilet rooms on each floor, having the number of plumbing fixtures as specified in Table 403.1 of this code for the classroom population of that floor.

worked_examples.how: 25 per sex; 1 per 25 for the first 50 = 1 each. Urinals may replace at most 50% of 1 = 0.5, so none.
50 per sex; 1 per 25 for the first 50 = 2 each. Urinals: at most 50% of 2 = 1.
100 per sex; first 50 at 1 per 25 = 2, remaining 50 at 1 per 50 = 1; 3 each. Urinals: at most 50% of 3 = 1.5, so 1.
200 per sex; first 50 = 2, remaining 150 at 1 per 50 = 3; 5 each. Urinals: at most 50% of 5 = 2.5, so 2.
25 per sex; 1 per 75 = 0.33, rounded up to 1 each. Urinals: at most 67% of 1, so none.
50 per sex; 1 per 75 = 0.67, rounded up to 1 each. Urinals: at most 67% of 1, so none.
100 per sex; 1 per 75 = 1.33, rounded up to 2 each. Urinals: at most 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 per sex; 1 per 75 = 2.67, rounded up to 3 each. Urinals: at most 67% of 3 = 2.01, so 2.
25 per sex; 1 per 50 = 0.5, rounded up to 1 each. Urinals: at most 67% of 1, so none.
50 per sex; 1 per 50 = 1 each. Urinals: at most 67% of 1, so none.
100 per sex; 1 per 50 = 2 each. Urinals: at most 67% of 2 = 1.34, so 1.
200 per sex; 1 per 50 = 4 each. Urinals: at most 67% of 4 = 2.68, so 2.

fixtures.confidence_note: Louisiana amendments read on the commission's own blue book (official). The table rows and Sections 403.1.1, 403.2, 405.3.4, 405.3.5 and 424.2 were read on UpCodes' Louisiana copy because codes.iccsafe.org returned HTTP 403.

hdpe_fire.section: IBC 2021 Section 803.9, adopted in Louisiana without amendment (LAC 17:I.103 amends no part of Chapter 8)
hdpe_fire.quote: 803.9 High-Density Polyethylene (HDPE) and Polypropylene (PP). Where high-density polyethylene or polypropylene is used as an interior finish, it shall comply with Section 803.1.1. | 803.1.1 Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish Materials Tested in Accordance With NFPA 286. Interior wall and ceiling finish materials shall be classified in accordance with NFPA 286 and comply with Section 803.1.1.1. | Chapter 2 definition, Interior Wall and Ceiling Finish: The exposed interior surfaces of buildings, including but not limited to: fixed or movable walls and partitions; toilet room privacy partitions; columns; ceilings; ...
hdpe_fire.note: Section text read on UpCodes' Louisiana copy; the absence of a Louisiana amendment to Chapter 8 was checked on the official blue book. Cities cannot amend it.

access.state_standard: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design (the ADA-ABA Accessibility Guidelines), reviewed and enforced by the Louisiana Office of State Fire Marshal. Louisiana's building code repeals IBC Sections 1103 to 1112 and lets commercial buildings follow the 2010 ADA Standards, so ICC A117.1 is not the working standard for stalls today.

no_difference_evidence.quote: Adopt Section 1102, Compliance. Amend Section 1102.1, Design. Adopt Exception: Until such time the 2024 edition of this code is adopted for use, commercial buildings shall be permitted to comply with the requirements of the 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design as adopted by the United States Department of Justice. Repeal Section 1103, Scoping Requirements ... Repeal Section 1112, Signage
Since October 1, 2011, the office has reviewed and enforced the 2010 ADA-ABA Accessibility Guidelines, as state law requires (page summary; the fetch tool would not return the page verbatim).
213.1 ALL toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be accessible and in compliance with Chapter 6 ... 604.8 Wheelchair accessible toilet compartments shall meet the requirements of 604.8.1 through ...

access.process: The State Fire Marshal reviews plans for every building to be constructed, renovated or repaired, or whose occupancy changes, except one- and two-family dwellings, and checks them against the 2010 ADA rules as part of that review. Its page: 'A Plan Review is required for all buildings to be constructed, renovated, repaired or the occupancy changed.' and 'If you have any concern as to whether a modification requires plan review, write a letter to this office addressed to the Plan Review Division.' The office can grant case-by-case accessibility appeals from the state requirement; these do not override federal law. No official page says whether a like-for-like partition replacement counts as a renovation needing review.
access.scheduled_change: The Louisiana exception that allows the 2010 ADA Standards is worded 'Until such time the 2024 edition of this code is adopted for use'. The 2024 editions are scheduled for 2027-01-01. Whether the 2024 adoption keeps the ADA route or brings in IBC Chapter 11 with ICC A117.1 was not read.

single_user.rule: Single-user toilet rooms count toward the required fixtures and must be identified as available to everyone regardless of sex. No stall is needed in a single-occupant room with a lockable door.
single_user.quote: 403.1.2 ... Single-user toilet and bathing rooms, and family or assisted-use toilet rooms and bathing rooms shall be identified as being available for use by all persons regardless of their sex.

all_gender_shared.rule: Allowed under the state code, with a Louisiana amendment: the fixture count is based on the whole occupant load, each toilet needs a compartment with a door, and each urinal must be in its own room with floor-to-ceiling walls and a solid door (a urinal screen is not enough). Rooms designed for both sexes must be enclosed by floor-to-ceiling walls with a solid door.
all_gender_shared.quote: Where multiple-user facilities are designed to serve all genders, the minimum fixture count shall be calculated 100 percent, based on total occupant load. In such multiple-user facilities, each fixture type shall be in accordance with ICC A117.1 and each urinal that is provided shall be located in a room, created by walls from floor to ceiling, with a solid door. | Separate facilities shall not be required where rooms, created by walls from floor to ceiling, with a solid door, having both water closets and lavatory fixtures are designed for use by both sexes and privacy for water closets is provided in accordance with Section 405.3.4. Urinals shall be located in a room, created by walls from floor to ceiling, with a solid door.
all_gender_shared.cite: LAC 17:I.111, amendments to IPC 403.1.1 Exception 2 and 403.2 Exception 6

use_restrictions.rule: La. R.S. 9:55 to 9:65 (Acts 2024, No. 436, in force August 1, 2024 per the search result; date not read on the statute page). Public schools, domestic violence shelters, correctional facilities and juvenile detention facilities must designate each multi-occupancy restroom for females, males or members of the same family, and a restroom designated for one sex may be used only by that sex. Single-occupancy restrooms not designated by sex remain allowed. The sections read do not cover private buildings or other government buildings.
use_restrictions.quote: R.S. 9:62(A): A public school shall designate each multi-occupancy restroom or changing room for the exclusive use of either females, males, or members of the same family. B.(1) A restroom or changing room within a public school that is designated for males or females shall be used only by members of that same sex. | R.S. 9:60: Nothing in this Part shall prohibit a domestic violence shelter, public school, correctional facility, or juvenile detention facility from: (1) Establishing single-occupancy restrooms, changing rooms, or sleeping quarters that are not designated by sex.

public_wage.law: None. Louisiana repealed its prevailing wage law in 1988. Only the federal Davis-Bacon Act applies, on federally funded work.
public_wage.quote: Louisiana - repealed in 1988. (U.S. Department of Labor, Dollar Threshold Amount for Contract Coverage, section 'States without Prevailing Wage Laws'; page last revised January 1, 2023)
public_wage.note: Federal page dated 2023; no Louisiana page was read confirming that no law has been enacted since.

state_rate_quote.quote: Rate Type; Rate as of January 1, 2025. Sales Tax; 5.00% ... Sales and use taxes levied by political subdivisions of the state are in addition to the sales and use taxes levied by the state.

shipped_goods.rule: Taxable. A seller with no physical presence in Louisiana must register with the Louisiana Sales and Use Tax Commission for Remote Sellers and collect state and local tax at the actual rates once its sales delivered into Louisiana pass $100,000 in the previous or current calendar year. If the seller does not collect, the buyer owes use tax.
shipped_goods.quote: Remote Sellers are required to collect and remit use tax if during the previous or current calendar year they have gross revenue in excess of $100,000 from sales of tangible personal property delivered into Louisiana or 200 or more separate transactions for delivery into Louisiana. ... Beginning July 1, 2020, Remote Sellers are required to collect and remit state and local sales and use tax based upon actual applicable bases and rates. | Use tax is due on all taxable sales transactions when the sales tax was not collected by the selling vendor.
shipped_goods.note: The commission's FAQ still lists a 200-transaction test; it may be out of date. Only the $100,000 test is used in page text.

freight.quote: Transportation charges paid to a seller for the delivery of tangible personal property or digital products purchased from that seller are subject to Louisiana state and local sales and use taxes. This applies regardless of whether the charges are separately stated or included in the total price.
freight.note: Revenue Information Bulletin 25-025, October 1, 2025. A bulletin is informal guidance. If the underlying sale is exempt, the freight is too.

install_labor.rule: Not taxable: labor to construct, install, remodel or repair immovable (real) property is generally not subject to Louisiana sales tax. Where labor is part of a sale of taxable goods, it should be stated separately on the invoice.
install_labor.quote: Labor to construct, install, remodel, or repair immovable (real) property is generally not subject to Louisiana sales tax. Examples include work performed on buildings, homes, permanently installed fixtures, and other real property improvements. ... Certain installation, application, remodeling, or repair labor may not be taxable if the labor charges are separately stated on the invoice as provided by Louisiana law. [table] Installing a permanent fixture to real property: Generally No

furnish_and_install.rule: The contractor is treated as the user of the materials and owes the tax on what it buys; the contract for work on the building is not itself taxed. On state or local government jobs the contractor still owes tax on materials unless the agency names it as its agent (form R-1020).
furnish_and_install.quote: Sales of tangible personal property, including materials, supplies, and equipment, made to contractors, or their contractors, subcontractors, or agents, for use in the construction, alteration, or repair of immovable property are presumed to be sales to consumers or users, not sales for resale, and therefore the contractor is liable for the taxes imposed by this Chapter on their purchases or importations of such tangible personal property.
furnish_and_install.note: The Department proposed amendments to LAC 61:I.4372 in 2026 (notice of intent dated 07.10.26 on its site); not read, status unknown.

page.stalls_intro: Louisiana's rules count toilets by a building's capacity: the most people it is designed to hold at one time, worked out from its floor area. Half are counted as men and half as women, and fractions round up. Every toilet needs a stall with a door. Urinals are optional: in each men's room they may replace up to half of the toilets, or up to two thirds in restaurants and schools, and each urinal needs a privacy screen.
page.stalls_after: These are minimums for the whole building, the same statewide because Louisiana cities and parishes enforce the state rules without changing them. At least one stall in each room must be wheelchair accessible. In a school, boys' and girls' restrooms must be on every floor and within 200 feet of each classroom door for children up to age 12, or 400 feet in a secondary school.
page.capacity: To find your building's capacity, the building rules count an office at one person per 150 square feet of floor, a restaurant dining room at one per 15 square feet and a classroom at one per 20.
page.fire_bullet: - **Fire safety:** Louisiana's building rules require solid plastic (HDPE) partitions to pass a room fire test. Ask for the fire-rated version.
page.access_bullet: - **Wheelchair access:** a restroom with stalls needs at least one stall a wheelchair user can enter and use. Federal law sets the sizes, and Louisiana enforces the same federal rules: the State Fire Marshal reviews plans for commercial buildings that are built, renovated or repaired. Ask its Plan Review Division whether your project needs a review.
page.state_extra_bullet: - **Louisiana and federal stall rules match:** Louisiana uses the federal access rules for stalls, doors and grab bars, so a stall that meets one meets the other.
page.restroom_bullet: - **Single-user and all-gender restrooms:** a one-person restroom must be marked as open to everyone. A shared all-gender room is allowed if every toilet sits in its own compartment with a door and every urinal is in its own room with full-height walls and a solid door. Since 2024, Louisiana law requires public schools, domestic violence shelters, jails and juvenile detention centers to designate each shared restroom for females, males or members of the same family.
page.public_jobs: Louisiana has no state wage law for public construction, so a required wage applies only on federally funded jobs, at the rate the U.S. Department of Labor sets for the parish.
page.tax_install_bullet: - **Tax on installation:** in Louisiana, labor to install, remodel or repair part of a building is generally not taxed. The installer pays the tax on the materials it buys for the job.
page.tax_ship_bullet: - **Buying without installation:** partitions shipped to {city} are taxable, freight included. If the seller doesn't collect the tax, the buyer owes it.
page.tax_confirm: your accountant or the Louisiana Department of Revenue

page.official_names: Accessibility: 2010 ADA Standards for Accessible Design (ADA-ABA Accessibility Guidelines), enforced by the Louisiana Office of State Fire Marshal. Building: Louisiana State Uniform Construction Code, International Building Code, 2021 Edition, with Louisiana amendments (LAC 17:I.103). Plumbing: International Plumbing Code, 2021 Edition, with Louisiana amendments (LAC 17:I.111). The 2024 editions are scheduled to take effect on January 1, 2027.
